segments.narration_text: A proposal can be right about the customer and still arrive in the wrong form. The team sees the research. Finance sees an unpriced commitment. Engineering sees work that may displace a promised upgrade. The person presenting keeps adding evidence, but no one has named the decision that each listener is being asked to carry. Chapter Sixteen describes that kind of meeting.

segments.narration_text: Imagine operations says, “We cannot spare staff to watch a long session.” Do not answer by repeating why the customer problem matters. Ask which part of the observation creates the burden. Could the test use fewer sessions, a shorter window, or an existing research appointment? If none is feasible, stop and redesign the test.
